verdict.rationale: Honeycomb documents threshold-based Triggers and SLO burn alerts, with notifications routed to Slack, PagerDuty, Microsoft Teams, or custom webhooks that accept JSON payloads. That covers the alerting and routing parts of the story. The evidence never mentions grouping or silencing of notifications, and it only implies that alerts can fire on all signal types (traces, logs, metrics). missing for 10: notification grouping, silencing/muting of alerts, explicit confirmation that triggers work on any telemetry signal type, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an SRE, I can alert on any telemetry signal with routing, grouping, and silencing of notifications

citations.quote: Use triggers to send alerts when thresholds that you define and configure are passed.
Set up Triggers and SLOs to alert your team when conditions are met, and route notifications to Slack, PagerDuty, Microsoft Teams, or a custom webhook.
Route Honeycomb Trigger and SLO burn alerts to any service that accepts a JSON payload, including third-party tools and custom integrations.
